title: The teacher under the tree
hook: a minister carrying a king's gold meets a teacher under a tree, and never buys the horses
carry: the teacher is the way: gurur upayah
tomorrow: who is the fierce one with the dog at Shiva's door?

segments.voice: Yesterday: one consciousness plays every part, even a lazy laborer who took a king's cane. Today, the man that flood came for, and how he found his teacher.

The Pandya king of Madurai gives his chief minister a fortune in gold and one job: ride to the coast and buy the finest horses. On the way, at a place called Tirupperunturai, the minister hears chanting. Under a tree sits a teacher, with students around him, perfectly calm. The minister gets down from his horse. He meant to stop for a moment. He falls at the teacher's feet instead, the teacher blesses him, and something in him opens. He never buys the horses.
screen: `A KING'S GOLD, FOR HORSES.` → `A TEACHER UNDER A TREE.` → `HE NEVER BUYS THE HORSES.`

segments.voice: The minister became Manikkavasagar, one of the great poet-saints of Tamil Shaivism; the name means the one whose words are gems. He spent the king's gold on a temple and on Shiva's devotees, and paid for it: the king had him punished, and in the Madurai telling, yesterday's flood and the laborer who took the cane came for his sake. And the teacher under the tree? Tradition says it was Shiva himself, come as a guru. Now the Shiva Sutras: gurur upayah. Guru is a teacher. Upaya is a means, the thing that gets you there. The teacher is the way. This book has said you are consciousness, that small knowing binds, that the self is a dancer who can forget who's dancing. If that's the problem, more information won't fix it. It's a habit of seeing, and habits change through someone who has seen. The commentator Kshemaraja reads the line more widely still: the guru is also Shiva's own grace, his power to reveal, working through a person. That's the teaching under a very Hindu habit. It's why students touch a teacher's feet, why many keep Guru Purnima, a full-moon day for honoring teachers, and why a mantra is traditionally received from a teacher, not copied off a page. Grace tends to arrive with a face. And the student still walks: Manikkavasagar still had to get down from his horse. So if something matters to you, a chant, a prayer, an instrument, find the person who can hand it over.
screen: `MANIKKAVASAGAR: WORDS LIKE GEMS.` · `THE GURU WAS SHIVA. GURUR UPAYAH.` · `A HABIT OF SEEING, HANDED ON.` · `SHIVA'S GRACE, THROUGH A PERSON.` · then, large: `THE TEACHER IS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Do what many Hindus do for a teacher. Bring to mind someone who showed you a way: a parent at the stove, a coach, a teacher who stayed after class. Let their face come, put your palms together, and bow your head toward them, a silent thank-you. If you pray, thank Shiva for the grace that came through them. If you don't, the thank-you is enough.
Gurur upayah. The teacher is the way: in Kashmir Shaivism, the guru, and Shiva's grace working through one.
Your line: the teacher is the way, gurur upayah. Grace tends to arrive with a face. Same time tomorrow.

howItsDone: Students of Kashmir Shaivism learn the Shiva Sutras from a teacher, line by line; many Hindus honor their teachers by touching their feet, and on Guru Purnima, the full-moon day for teachers.
